answer: Each agent vertex can be registered only by locking a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually released as the agent completes independently sampled tasks. A network of reviewers checks each task, with disagreements triggering a costly recheck; repeated agreement between the same identities does not count as independent evidence. An attacker who creates many sybils must therefore tie up more real capital and pay for distinct work and review, while risking forfeiture for fabricated results. A mesa of identities cannot cheaply wander into trust just by being numerous.
